html:
The Kungarakany, also spelt Kungarakan, are an Aboriginal Australian people of the Northern Territory, in the country of the Adelaide and Finniss rivers south of Darwin. The map shows them from 1600 to 1815. European settlers called them the Paperbark People.

Their neighbours were the Larrakia to the north, the Malak-Malak to the southwest, the Wagiman to the south and the Limilngan to the east. After the founding of Darwin in 1869, the railway south to Pine Creek and the mining and farming along it ran through their land. Their language now has very few speakers.
